title: IDFC First Bank Ltd - 539437 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IDFC First Bank Q1 FY27 profit crossed INR1,000 crore for first time at INR1,075 crore (+132% YoY); credit cost guidance cut to 150-160 bps.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 profit rose to INR1,075 crore, up about 132% YoY, with NII up 21.1% YoY and loans up 20.6% YoY to about INR3.05 lakh crore. Asset quality improved further, with GNPA at 1.51% and NNPA at 0.44%, and the bank booked a voluntary INR515 crore contingency provision. Management raised its FY27 ROA ambition to about 1%, lowered its credit cost guidance and kept the cost-to-income target under 70% through the year. Margin guidance was trimmed slightly to around 5.8% from 5.75%.

+16.4% YoY; +2.3% QoQ ex Q4 fraud one-off

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: Book about INR2.4 lakh crore, up about 18% YoY; GNPA 1.40% (-7 bps QoQ), NNPA 0.52% (-4 bps QoQ). Gross slippages down 30% YoY and net slippages down 44% YoY.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Book about INR64,000 crore, up about 30% YoY.

segments.name: Microfinance
segments.commentary: Book about INR6,700 crore, marginally up QoQ; 93% covered under CGFMU; SMA 1+2 at 0.71%.

segments.name: Credit cards
segments.commentary: Book about INR9,600 crore (+19% YoY), 4.8 million cards in force, spends up 22% YoY.

segments.name: Wealth management
segments.commentary: AUM about INR64,000 crore, up 24% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Customer deposits just under INR3 lakh crore, +16.6% YoY and +5.3% QoQ. CASA at INR1.58 lakh crore, CASA ratio 50.8% (+1 pt QoQ). NRI deposits about INR25,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA now expected at about 1%, versus earlier 'kissing distance' framing; management said it is gunning for about 1% for the full year.

FY27 NIM now seen at about 5.8%, up from earlier 5.75% guide, but pressured by asset mix shift and possible normalisation of the investment book; cost of funds seen range-bound around 6%. No rate hike assumed.
FY27 credit cost cut to 150-160 bps from 170-180 bps earlier.
Opex growth guidance of 13-14% for the year retained; management aims to keep at least a 500 bps positive jaw (income growth minus opex growth).
Cost to income ratio targeted below 70% during the year, from 70.7% in Q1.
MFI book growth target of about 15% YoY through the year as disbursements pick up.
FCNR(B) share target of about 2.5% of an assumed USD 60-70 billion inflow, versus about 1.7% share of the NRI deposit market today; FCNR rate of 6.75%.
ECL transition impact on capital expected to be broadly neutral, with higher provisions partly offset by RWA relief and EIR benefits; run-rate impact described as manageable, no numbers given.
Structural ROA ambition of about 1.7-1.8% over time, described as not a formal guidance.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed.
Technology: IT expense down to about 9% of opex from about 11%; management said the bank is building a modern cloud, API-first and event-driven stack.
PSL: about INR1.2 lakh crore of PSL assets, but still a net buyer of PSLCs; last year's PSLC loss about INR250 crore.
demand_pricing: Loan growth 20.6% YoY, led by mortgage, vehicle, corporate and consumer loans; wholesale growth 30%, retail/agri/MSME 18%.
Disbursements up more than 25% YoY in Q1; MFI disbursements nearly doubled YoY.
Fee income up 22.9% YoY, with trade, FX and commercial banking fees contributing.
Channel sourcing expense about 20% of opex, range-bound; expected to grow in line with volumes.
Management said corporate NIM is lower than retail, so more corporate lending dilutes NIM.

Deposit recovery after the earlier fraud episode: management said deposits were flat in the quarter and have since returned strongly; institutional deposits described as stable. Average CA deposits up about 30% YoY and SA up about 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall from 5.9% to 5.75% for the full year, and what is the rate-hike sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects FY27 margin around 5.8%, citing asset mix shift and investment book normalisation, with cost of funds range-bound near 6%. No rate hike was factored in.

qa_highlights.question: Can credit cost guidance come down given Q1 at 153 bps, and are EWS signals turning negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance cut to 150-160 bps from 170-180 bps. Asset quality indicators are trending well; the INR515 crore contingency provision is a prudent buffer for geopolitical and monsoon risks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition and run-rate impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital impact on transition expected to be broadly neutral. Run-rate provisions will be higher, partly offset by EIR amortisation of sourcing and processing fees. No specific number given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FCNR(B) targets and mobilisation to date?
qa_highlights.answer: Target about 2.5% of an assumed USD 60-70 billion pool, versus about 1.7% of the INR1.65 trillion NRI deposit market today. Mobilisation has just started; no figure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is opex growth still 13-14%, and will the jaw be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep at least a 500 bps jaw; the opex range depends on business momentum. Next year, a similar jaw is expected to cut cost to income by about 350 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Any fraud recoveries in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: No recovery booked in Q1. Legal process is under way with arrests, an ED charge sheet and PMLA court claims; no timeline given.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from asset mix shift, a possible investment book normalisation, and FCNR cost; FY27 NIM guide of about 5.8%.
Sustainability of credit cost at 150-160 bps, which relies on the contingency buffer and macro/monsoon/geopolitical factors.
ECL transition from next year: higher provisions and capital effects still being fine-tuned.
Fraud recovery timing is uncertain and recoveries are not in the P&L.
Whether the cost to income ratio can get below 70% and whether opex growth stays within 13-14% as the business grows.
Dependence on the CGFMU scheme for MFI; the claim is annual, and future amounts are expected to be much smaller.
Deposit mix: management aims to shift toward retail deposits from institutional deposits.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, asset quality and deposit recovery, with clear upgrades to ROA and credit cost. Management was more cautious on margin (lowered to about 5.8%) and on the timing of recoveries and ECL, and it leaned heavily on qualitative messaging about governance and customer-first culture.
key_quotes: Happy to report that we have crossed profit of INR1,000 crores for the first time and the profit for the quarter stands at INR1,075 crores
we think that our bank is structurally built for a ROA of more like 1.7 %, 1.8% as it builds out.
we feel now we could land up more with 150 to 160 basis points on credit cost.
So, let me directly at my level let me assure you, there is absolutely no problem on deposits; in fact we are flying actually.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 ROA about 1%, NIM about 5.8%, credit cost 150-160 bps (cut) and opex growth 13-14% with a 500 bps jaw, backed by loan growth of 20.6% and disbursements up over 25%, but no capacity or capex figures were given and no revenue growth guide was stated.
